fable.w: This provision only rescinds previously appropriated funds. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. There is no tempting opposite reading, because the text is purely a fiscal rescission with no decision-making process.
fable.s: Of the funds made available under this heading in Public Law 103–317, $5,000,000 are rescinded.

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple appropriation provision that rescinds (cancels) a specific amount of funding. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or requirements for outside input mentioned.
qwen_block.s: Of the funds made available under this heading in Public Law 103–317, $5,000,000 are rescinded.

opus.w: This provision only rescinds previously appropriated funds. It involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue, so no outside party takes part in any federal decision. Nothing in the text could reasonably be read as participation.
opus.s: Of the funds made available under this heading in Public Law 103–317, $5,000,000 are rescinded.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply rescinds a specific amount of appropriated funds. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities). It is a unilateral budgetary action by Congress.
qwen_chat.s: Of the funds made available under this heading in Public Law 103–317, $5,000,000 are rescinded.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that rescinding funds is a "decision" and therefore any process leading to it involves participation. However, the text itself contains no mention of any process, consultation, hearing, or interaction with outside parties. It is a unilateral legislative action regarding budget numbers.
